To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the merger rate in the A901 clusters at z = 0.165 is low, (2) the merger fraction increases with distance from the cluster center, and (3) mergers are preferentially blue, and their average SFR is enhanced.

the merger fraction in clusters and groups is low, that the merger frequency is highest at the outskirts of clusters, that the majority of the merger population in clusters is blue, and that mergers in clusters contribute to only a small fraction (∼10%–15%) of the SFR in clusters.

the merger rate in the A901 clusters is similar to that of field galaxies and that the merger-induced star formation in these clusters contributes a small fraction of the total star formation in the cluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the frequency and properties of interacting galaxies in the Abell clusters A901 and A902 at a redshift of 0.165.
the merger fraction in clusters, the influence of environment on mergers, and the impact of mergers on the SFR in clusters.
the merger fraction, its evolution with redshift, its dependence on environment, and the impact of mergers on galaxy colors and SFR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the merger fraction in A901/902 is consistent with the predictions from N-body simulations of the accretion of groups onto clusters.
mergers contribute to the star formation activity in clusters, but they do not dominate the star formation in the clusters.
the fraction of mergers in clusters is low, and the merger rate is not sufficient to account for the observed SFR density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the merger fraction of intermediate-mass galaxies is low, and the fraction of mergers in clusters is comparable to those in field groups.
mergers contribute only a small amount (∼10%) of the total star formation in clusters.
the A901/02 supercluster is in a transition stage between a group of galaxies and a cluster, with the merger fraction and the SFR density of the supercluster similar to those in groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mergers are rare events in the A901 clusters, and that the bulk of the star formation in clusters is driven by galaxies which are not undergoing a merger.
the A901/900 supercluster is still accreting galaxies from its surroundings, which may be the cause for the observed high merger fraction.
mergers in the field and in clusters contribute only a minor fraction of the SFR in clusters at z ∼0.17, and the majority of the SFR comes from non-interactions.
